To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

for a large class of games with continuous payoff functions, there does not necessarily exist a Nash equilibrium, and that the existence of a Nash equilibrium depends critically on the shape of the reaction functions of firms.

(i) for an open and large subset of the space of reaction corre- spondences, there does not exists a Nash equilibrium, (ii) the same result holds for a large and open subset of the space continuous objective functions, (iii) the set of objective functions that do have a pure strategy Nash equilibria are dense in the space of all objective functions.

the existence of pure strategy equilibria is not guaranteed in the space of reaction functions and that an open and dense set of continuous objective functions does not have a pure strategy Nash equilibria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of existence of Nash equilibrium in a general setting.
the question of the extent to which the existence of a Nash equilibrium is robust with respect to perturbations of objective functions.
the question: what is the probability that a Nash equilibrium exists in a given class of games?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the existence of a Nash equilibrium is not guaranteed if one of the following two conditions is not met: (1) the objective function is quasi-concave and (2) the set of strategies is compact.
the existence of a Nash equilibrium is an exception rather than the rule.
if the space of reaction correspondence is open, then the set of Nash equilibria has empty interior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the assumption of quasi- concavity of objectives cannot be dropped without losing the existence of Nash equilibria in pure strategies.
the existence of pure strategy Nash equilibria in games with continuous payoff functions is not generic.
for the class of reaction correspondences we consider, there is no pure strategy Nash equilibrium in a large subset of the space of continuous objectives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the assumption of quasi concavity of objectives is not a necessary one for the existence of Nash equilibrium.
the assumption that the space of continuous functions is dense in the space of all functions is a strong assumption.
the assumption of quasiconcavity is a very strong one and that dropping it leads to the conclusion that the existence of Nash equilibria is a very special property.
